q: In a titration, 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution is exactly neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid (NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O). What is the concentration of the sodium hydroxide?
explain: Moles of HCl = 0.100 × 0.0200 = 0.00200 mol. The ratio is 1 : 1, so NaOH = 0.00200 mol in 0.0250 dm³, giving 0.0800 mol/dm³.

q: What is the formula of sulfuric acid?
explain: Sulfuric acid contains two hydrogen atoms, one sulfur atom and four oxygen atoms: H₂SO₄. H₂SO₃ is sulfurous acid and H₂S is hydrogen sulfide.

q: An element has two isotopes: 50.0% is atoms of mass number 79 and 50.0% is atoms of mass number 81. What is its relative atomic mass?
Which statement describes the relative atomic mass, Ar, of an element?
options: The mass of one atom of the element in grams
The mass of the most common isotope compared with 1/12th of the mass of an atom of carbon-12
The average mass of the isotopes of the element compared with 1/12th of the mass of an atom of carbon-12
The number of protons and neutrons in the most common isotope
explain: Ar uses the average mass of all the naturally occurring isotopes of the element, compared with 1/12th of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

q: A hydrocarbon has the empirical formula C₂H₅ and a relative molecular mass of 58. What is its molecular formula? (Ar: H = 1, C = 12)
explain: The empirical formula mass is 29, and 58 ÷ 29 = 2, so the molecular formula is (C₂H₅)₂ = C₄H₁₀.

q: Boron has two isotopes: 20% is boron-10 and 80% is boron-11. What is the relative atomic mass of boron?
A model of a compound shows one calcium atom, one carbon atom and three oxygen atoms bonded together. What is the formula of the compound?
explain: The numbers of atoms are Ca 1, C 1 and O 3, so the formula is CaCO₃.

q: Which statement about the relative molecular mass, Mr, of a substance is correct?
options: It has no units because it is a comparison with 1/12th of the mass of a carbon-12 atom
explain: Mr is a ratio of masses, so it has no units. Molar mass (the mass of one mole) has units of g/mol.

q: Aluminium forms Al³⁺ ions and oxygen forms O²⁻ ions. What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
explain: The charges must balance: 2 × (+3) = +6 and 3 × (−2) = −6, so the ratio is Al : O = 2 : 3.

q: What is the relative molecular mass, Mr, of ethanol, C₂H₅OH? (Ar: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
An iron oxide contains 5.6 g of iron and 2.4 g of oxygen. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: O = 16, Fe = 56)
Which ionic equation is balanced for both atoms and charge?
explain: The left side has charge +2 and 2 H atoms; the right side has Mg²⁺ (+2) and H₂ (2 H atoms). The other equations have unequal charge or atoms.

q: A solution contains 20 g of solute dissolved in 2 dm³ of solution. What is its concentration in g/dm³?
explain: Concentration = mass ÷ volume = 20 g ÷ 2 dm³ = 10 g/dm³.

q: How many particles are there in one mole of any substance?
explain: One mole contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles (atoms, ions or molecules). This is the Avogadro constant.

q: Which word equation shows the complete combustion of methane?
explain: Methane is a hydrocarbon. Burning it in plenty of oxygen forms carbon dioxide and water.

q: Which statement defines the empirical formula of a compound?
options: The number and type of different atoms in one molecule
The simplest whole number ratio of the different atoms or ions in the compound
The mass of each element in 100 g of the compound
The total relative mass of all the atoms in the compound
explain: The empirical formula gives only the simplest whole number ratio of atoms or ions, for example CH₂ for C₄H₈ or Na₂O for the ionic compound with ions in a 2:1 ratio.

q: Magnesium forms Mg²⁺ ions and nitrate is NO₃⁻. What is the formula of magnesium nitrate?
explain: One Mg²⁺ (+2) needs two NO₃⁻ (−1 each), and the nitrate group goes in brackets: Mg(NO₃)₂.

q: In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, 4 g of hydrogen forms 36 g of water. What mass of water forms from 1 g of hydrogen in excess oxygen?
explain: 1 g is a quarter of 4 g, so the mass of water is a quarter of 36 g, which is 9 g.

q: Aqueous silver nitrate is mixed with aqueous sodium chloride and a white precipitate forms. Which ionic equation represents the reaction?
explain: Only silver ions and chloride ions combine to make the solid silver chloride. Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ stay in solution and are not included.

q: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. What mass of iron forms from 80 g of iron(III) oxide? (Ar: O = 16, Fe = 56)
explain: Mr of Fe₂O₃ = 160, so 80 g = 0.50 mol. The ratio Fe₂O₃ : Fe is 1 : 2, so 1.0 mol of Fe = 56 g.

q: Which row correctly matches a quantity with its unit?
explain: Amount of substance is measured in mol. Molar mass is in g/mol, concentration in g/dm³ or mol/dm³ and molar gas volume in dm³/mol.

q: Carbon burns in oxygen: 12 g of carbon forms 44 g of carbon dioxide. What mass of carbon dioxide forms from 3 g of carbon?
explain: 3 g is a quarter of 12 g, so the carbon dioxide formed is a quarter of 44 g, which is 11 g.

q: Aqueous silver nitrate reacts with aqueous sodium chloride. Which ions are spectator ions?
explain: Spectator ions are present but do not change. Ag⁺ and Cl⁻ form the AgCl precipitate, but Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ stay dissolved.

q: A solution of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, has a concentration of 0.50 mol/dm³. What is its concentration in g/dm³? (Ar: H = 1, O = 16, S = 32)
explain: Mr of H₂SO₄ = 98. Concentration in g/dm³ = 0.50 × 98 = 49 g/dm³.

q: What is the mass of 0.20 mol of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (Ar: H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)
explain: Molar mass of NaOH = 40 g/mol. Mass = moles × molar mass = 0.20 × 40 = 8.0 g.

q: A student needs to convert a volume of 250 cm³ to dm³. What is the volume in dm³?
2Al₂O₃ → 4Al + 3O₂. What mass of aluminium forms from 204 g of aluminium oxide? (Ar: O = 16, Al = 27)
explain: Mr of Al₂O₃ = 102, so 204 g = 2.0 mol. The ratio Al₂O₃ : Al is 1 : 2, so 4.0 mol of Al = 4.0 × 27 = 108 g.

q: Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). Excess acid is added to 6.5 g of zinc. What volume of hydrogen forms at r.t.p.? (Ar: Zn = 65; molar gas volume = 24 dm³)
explain: 6.5 g ÷ 65 g/mol = 0.10 mol of Zn gives 0.10 mol of H₂. Volume = 0.10 × 24 = 2.4 dm³.

q: Why is the relative atomic mass of an element often not a whole number?
options: Atoms contain a fraction of a proton
The mass of the electrons is added to the mass of the nucleus
The mass of an atom cannot be measured exactly
It is an average over the isotopes present, taking their abundances into account
explain: Different isotopes have different mass numbers, and Ar is the weighted average of these, which is usually not a whole number.

q: What is the volume of 0.50 mol of a gas at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.)?
explain: One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ at r.t.p., so 0.50 mol occupies 0.50 × 24 = 12 dm³.
